# Scope clarification and synthesis

Read after reconstructing the relevant past work or completing a live demonstration. This phase chooses the future job to be encoded; it is not an invitation to replay the task.

## Recommend a concrete target

Briefly describe the important path and one likely reusable boundary. When appropriate, distinguish the full workflow from a recurring subworkflow or a decision protocol. Explain the useful exclusions.

For example, a completed investigation may contain a one-time reinstall, recurring service setup, and a reusable verification. These are different potential skills. Do not combine them automatically because they appeared in the same conversation.

Check a known relevant existing skill or project procedure if it may already cover the request. Keep this comparison bounded. No broad marketplace search or new authoring dependency is mandatory.

## Ask questions that affect the artifact

Questions should be tied to actual choices from the run. Usually one small batch is sufficient. Use the dimensions below selectively, not as a form.

| Decision | Focused question pattern |
| --- | --- |
| Scope | Should this cover first-time setup too, or only the recurring check? |
| Exclusions | Was the reinstall a one-off recovery that should stay out of normal runs? |
| Inputs | Should this accept another service endpoint, or remain specific to this project? |
| Preference | Was the naming choice a standing convention or just for this output? |
| Human boundary | Keep authentication as a user step, or use an already approved integration when available? |
| Verification | Is a successful response sufficient, or should the skill also check its contents? |
| Future invocation | Should this generated skill require explicit invocation or be available for relevant requests? |
| Delivery | Deliver a reviewable artifact, create it in a named source directory, or update an identified existing skill? |

Do not ask when the answer is already supplied. A complete invocation can settle all material choices without another turn. If the user delegates defaults, choose narrowly and state material assumptions. Prefer inert delivery and no additional permissions. Propose explicit invocation for the initial generated draft when policy is unspecified; that is a changeable default, not an inherited universal rule.

Distinguish facts from preferences. A user who now asks for a different future success criterion has changed the specification, not the historical outcome. Preserve that difference in the evidence account.

After answers settle scope, author. Do not add a second request for permission to create the agreed artifact. A proposal-only instruction remains controlling.

## Evaluate usefulness without gatekeeping

A skill is valuable when it preserves a useful sequence, missed prerequisite, repeatable judgment, handoff, guard, preference, or verification. Repetition and convenience can justify a short skill. Complexity is not a requirement.

Recommend against unnecessary duplication or a skill dominated by temporary state. Explain the decisive reason briefly. The user may still select a narrow shortcut, an update to an existing skill, or a documentation artifact instead. Honor that choice within its scope.

## Compile a clean procedure

Keep the historical account separate from the reusable procedure. Classify values as requirements, inputs, environment-derived state, preferences, incidental values, or sensitive values to omit. Parameterize incidental values, but do not claim that an untested range of inputs already works.

For each material action or lesson, choose its role: a step, human handoff, prerequisite, branch, success check, stop condition, remedy, or omitted incidental detail. Failed steps should normally become lessons, not scheduled failures in future runs.

Reordering operations, introducing a preventative check, choosing another tool, or automating a formerly human action changes the procedure. Treat that change as proposed. A failure followed by several fixes does not prove which fix was necessary; preserve the uncertainty.

Do not transform a one-off user choice into a permanent preference without evidence or clarification. A human judgment that has no operational decision rule should remain a human decision rather than becoming a fabricated algorithm.

## Set the authoring contract

Before writing, know the selected purpose, inclusions and exclusions, varying inputs, human boundaries, success condition, evidence limits, future invocation policy, and authorized output. Do not force each field into a user-visible form.

The final skill should be usable by an agent without this session. Retain exact commands only when their behavior matters and is supported. Prefer state-based instructions where incidental mechanics do not matter, but avoid replacing a precise proven recipe with vague advice.

Proceed to `author-and-validate.md` in this directory. Do not stop at a candidate outline unless the user asked for one.
